From 0902010c8d163f7b62e655efda1a843529152c7c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Felix Gu <ustc.gu@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 18:07:59 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] regulator: fp9931: Fix PM runtime reference leak in
 fp9931_hwmon_read()

In fp9931_hwmon_read(), if regmap_read() failed, the function returned
the error code without calling pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(), causing
a PM reference leak.

Fixes: 12d821bd13d4 ("regulator: Add FP9931/JD9930 driver")
Signed-off-by: Felix Gu <ustc.gu@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Andreas Kemnade <andreas@kemnade.info>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260224-fp9931-v1-1-1cf05cabef4a@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/regulator/fp9931.c b/drivers/regulator/fp9931.c
index 7fbcc6327cc6..abea3b69d8a0 100644
--- a/drivers/regulator/fp9931.c
+++ b/drivers/regulator/fp9931.c
@@ -144,13 +144,12 @@ static int fp9931_hwmon_read(struct device *dev, enum hwmon_sensor_types type,
 		return ret;
 
 	ret = regmap_read(data->regmap, FP9931_REG_TMST_VALUE, &val);
-	if (ret)
-		return ret;
+	if (!ret)
+		*temp = (s8)val * 1000;
 
 	pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(data->dev);
-	*temp = (s8)val * 1000;
 
-	return 0;
+	return ret;
 }
 
 static umode_t fp9931_hwmon_is_visible(const void *data,
-- 
2.34.1

### Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a PM runtime reference leak in the `fp9931_hwmon_read()` function of the FP9931/JD9930 regulator driver.

**File modified:** `drivers/regulator/fp9931.c`

**Changes:**
- The original code returned an error immediately if `regmap_read()` failed, skipping the necessary `pm_runtime_put_autosuspend()` call. This caused a reference leak.
- The fix restructures the logic: `regmap_read()` is still called, but its return value is preserved. Only if it succeeds, the temperature value (`*temp`) is updated. Then, regardless of success or failure, `pm_runtime_put_autosuspend()` is called, and the function returns the error code from `regmap_read()`.

**Relationship:**
The restructuring ensures that the PM runtime reference is always released after the read attempt, even if the read itself fails. This eliminates the reference leak without changing the external behavior (the function still returns the error code on failure).

Here is the commit message:
regulator: fp9931: Fix PM runtime reference leak in
 fp9931_hwmon_read()

In fp9931_hwmon_read(), if regmap_read() failed, the function returned
the error code without calling pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(), causing
a PM reference leak.

Fixes: 12d821bd13d4 ("regulator: Add FP9931/JD9930 driver")
Signed-off-by: Felix Gu <ustc.gu@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Andreas Kemnade <andreas@kemnade.info>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260224-fp9931-v1-1-1cf05cabef4a@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
In fp9931_hwmon_read(), when regmap_read() returns a non-zero error, the function immediately returns that error without calling pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(). This causes a PM runtime reference leak because the function had previously called pm_runtime_get_sync() (which increments the usage count). The missing put keeps the device in an active state unnecessarily.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int fp9931_hwmon_read(struct device *dev, enum hwmon_sensor_types type,
 			     u32 attr, int channel, long *temp)
 {
 	struct fp9931_data *data = dev_get_drvdata(dev);
 	unsigned int val;
 	int ret;
 
 	ret = pm_runtime_resume_and_get(data->dev);
 	if (ret < 0)
 		return ret;
 
 	ret = regmap_read(data->regmap, FP9931_REG_TMST_VALUE, &val);
-	if (ret)
-		return ret;
+	if (!ret)
+		*temp = (s8)val * 1000;
 
 	pm_runtime_put_autosuspend(data->dev);
-	*temp = (s8)val * 1000;
 
-	return 0;
+	return ret;
 }
